items.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued October 30 at 6:19AM AKDT until October 30 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Visibility a quarter mile or less in dense fog.

* WHERE...Petersburg Borough.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM AKDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility could make travel conditions hazardous.
The combination of fog and icy surfaces is making travel extremely
hazardous.
items.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 30 at 5:01AM AKDT until October 31 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and 12
inches. Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range South of Trims Camp.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Areas of blowing snow could
reduce visibility.
items.areas: Eastern Alaska Range South of Trims Camp
items.instruction:

items.description:

items.headline: High Wind Warning issued October 30 at 4:29AM AKDT until October 30 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 30 to 45 mph with gusts up to 70 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Windy Pass.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest winds are likely through Friday
morning.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: High Wind Warning issued October 30 at 4:17AM AKDT until October 30 at 11:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 30 to 45 mph with gusts of 60 to 75 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River Hillsides. Strongest gusts will
likely be in the Bear Valley, Potter Creek, and Rabbit Creek areas.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM AKDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel will be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest winds will occur early this
morning, then steadily taper off through early this afternoon.
items.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind. Prepare for the possibility of power outages.
Use caution if you must travel.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 30 at 4:02AM AKDT until October 30 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Visibility one half mile or less at times.
Total snow accumulations 10 to 15 inches.

* WHERE...Thompson Pass.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The heaviest snow is expected through late
this afternoon. Warming temperatures through this afternoon will
lead to a changeover to rain for lower elevations of the pass. The
top of the pass will likely remain all snow.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

items.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 30 at 4:02AM AKDT until October 30 at 4:15PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by
excessive rainfall is possible.


* WHERE...Seward.

* WHEN...Until 415 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moderate rainfall will continue this morning before the rain
slowly tapers off later this afte
items.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

items.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 30 at 4:02AM AKDT until October 30 at 2:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Visibility one quarter mile or less at
times. Total snow accumulations 7 to 15 inches.

* WHERE...Northern Susitna Valley, including the Parks Highway
corridor through Broad Pass.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult, with low visibility and
rapidly accumulating snow along the Parks Highway.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Heavy snow will continue to fall through late
this morning. Snow could then mix with or change to rain F
items.instruction:
A Winter Storm Warning for snow means severe winter weather
conditions will make travel very hazardous. If you must travel, keep
an extra flashlight, food and water in your vehicle in case of an
emergency.

For the latest road conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 29 at 2:35PM AKDT until October 31 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Water levels of 2.5 to 3.5 feet above the normal high
tide expected during the Thursday and Friday high tides.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast, specifically Hooper Bay.

* WHEN...Until 1 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Beach property and lowest buildings may be impacted.
Multiple high tide cycles above normal may lead to localized
beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels of around 1 to 3 feet above
the normal high tide line are expected along the rest of the
Yukon Delta Coast.
items.instruction:
See weather.gov/afg for the latest updates. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.
